questions.question: What is a computer network?
options: A single computer connected to a printer
Two or more computers connected to share data and resources
questions.explanation: A network is two or more computers connected together to share data, files, and resources like printers.

questions.question: Which network type covers a single building like an office or school lab?
questions.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area like one building — office, school lab, or home.

questions.question: What does DNS stand for?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) converts website names like google.com into IP addresses that computers understand.

questions.question: Which network topology is most commonly used today?
questions.explanation: Star topology is most common — all devices connect to a central switch or router. Easy to add/remove devices.

questions.question: How many layers does the OSI model have?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to securely browse websites?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) encrypts data between your browser and the website. Always look for the lock icon.

questions.question: What does a router do?
options: Connects your network to the internet and directs traffic
questions.explanation: A router connects your local network to the internet and decides which path data should take.

questions.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
options: TCP is faster, UDP is slower
TCP confirms delivery, UDP just sends without confirmation
TCP is for WiFi, UDP is for cables
TCP is old, UDP is new
questions.explanation: TCP confirms every packet is received (reliable but slower). UDP just sends data without checking (faster, used for video calls and gaming).

questions.question: What is an IP address?
options: A unique number assigned to every device on a network
questions.explanation: An IP address (like 192.168.1.5) is a unique number that identifies each device on a network.

questions.question: Which cyber attack tricks you into giving your password through a fake email?
questions.explanation: Phishing uses fake emails or websites that look real to trick you into entering your password or personal info.

questions.question: What is the memory trick for OSI layers (top to bottom)?
options: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away
All People Seem To Need Data Processing
questions.explanation: All People Seem To Need Data Processing = Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical.

questions.question: What does a firewall do?
questions.explanation: A firewall monitors network traffic and blocks unauthorized access — like a security guard for your network.

questions.question: What is a VPN used for?
options: Creating a secure, encrypted connection over the internet
questions.explanation: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) encrypts all your internet traffic and hides your IP address. Important on public WiFi.

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles encryption?
questions.explanation: The Presentation layer (Layer 6) handles encryption, compression, and data format conversion (SSL/TLS, JPEG, etc.)

questions.question: What is a CDN?
options: A network that stores website copies in servers around the world for faster loading
questions.explanation: CDN (Content Delivery Network) stores copies of websites on servers worldwide. Your request goes to the nearest server for faster loading.
